one_line_contribution: It claims the raw-vs-distilled memory dispute is not about abstraction level but about two nameable content cues, scene bindings (object-to-receptacle facts, valuable only when the deployment scene recurs and harmful otherwise) and failure-to-repair pairs (scene-invariant), and it tests this by transplanting each cue into and out of six representations at matched injected-token budgets on ALFWorld seen/unseen room splits.
closest_prior_work: Three, all verified via s2cli. (1) SkillEvolBench, arXiv:2605.24117 (verified; 2026-05-22) is the paper the proposal is answering, and it is also the main novelty problem: its own abstract already attributes raw-trajectory superiority to 'discarded contextual cues'. The proposed contribution is therefore to name and localize an explanation that is already in print, not to propose a new one; a reviewer will ask what is left if the answer turns out to be exactly what SkillEvolBench already said. (2) Demystifying Agent Skills, arXiv:2608.14036 (verified; 2026-08-14) is the closest methodological threat: it is already a controlled contrastive study with paired trajectory analysis that attributes skill gains to procedural anchoring rather than knowledge injection, i.e. a mechanism-attribution study of the same dispute. It does not do the seen/unseen split, the token matching or the cue transplant, so it does not scoop the design, but it does occupy the 'we explain why skills work' slot and its procedural-anchoring account competes directly with the failure-to-repair arm (a repair pair may help simply as an anchor, regardless of its content). (3) Contextual Experience Replay, arXiv:2506.06698 (verified; ACL 2025, 47 citations) already partitions accumulated experience into environment-specific dynamics and transferable skills, with ablations on each part. That is essentially the proposal's bindings-vs-repairs dichotomy, one benchmark family over (WebArena rather than ALFWorld), which materially reduces the novelty of the taxonomy itself; what survives is the token-matched transplant and the seen/unseen asymmetry, not the idea that memory contains an environment-specific component and a transferable one. Also verified and relevant: Coarse-to-Fine Grounded Memory arXiv:2508.15305 (EMNLP 2025) grounds environment-level information for ALFWorld planning.
strongest_objection: The binding construct may not exist in ALFWorld the way the proposal needs it to. ALFWorld/ALFRED resamples object placements across episodes: the receptacle inventory and the room layout are fixed per room instance, but which receptacle holds the target object is randomized per task instance. If so, a 'scene binding' harvested from a training trajectory in room R is not valid for a different task instance in room R, and raw's seen-scene advantage cannot be mediated by bindings at all. What would survive is a receptacle-type prior ('mugs are in cabinets and on countertops'), which is exactly the kind of cue that transfers to unseen rooms as well, collapsing the predicted split-by-cue interaction into noise for reasons of environment design rather than of hypothesis. The proposal's Risk section worries about whether the unseen side has enough tasks, but never about whether within-room bindings are stable across task instances, and no experiment validates the binding annotation against the next episode's ground truth. A second, independent hit on the same arm: the P5 headline ('after conditioning on the two cue indicators the residual effect of representation is within noise') is a regression adjustment for a post-treatment mediator measured by a heuristic annotator that the proposal itself expects to miss paraphrased bindings inside abstract representations. Mediator measurement error causes under-adjustment, which manufactures exactly the residual representation effect that P5 is set up to reject, so a null on P5 and a positive on P5 are both explainable by annotation quality; the 200-item manual audit calibrates the annotator but does not correct the estimate.
what_would_fix_it: (a) Establish the binding construct before the confirmatory run: measure, on the local ALFWorld tasks, how often the object-to-receptacle pair recorded in a training trajectory still holds in a different task instance of the same room, and report that persistence rate. If it is low, redefine the cue as a receptacle-type prior and rewrite P2/P3, or move the seen/unseen contrast to an environment where scene state genuinely persists. (b) Add a cue-only representation (binding table alone, repair-pair list alone, both together) at the same 1,200-token budget; this is the direct test of 'the cues are the whole story' and it makes P5 an experimental comparison instead of a mediator regression. (c) Pre-register a multiplicity correction over the ~21 cells and six predictions, not just a per-comparison p<0.01. (d) Estimate the residual representation effect with the transplants as instruments or as a randomized within-item manipulation rather than by conditioning on an error-prone indicator, and report the annotator's measured sensitivity per representation so the adjustment can be corrected for attenuation. (e) Extend the transplant arms to R4/R6, since P5's falsification clause names skill and graph but only R1/R3/R5 get the machinery that could diagnose a residual there. (f) Add a step-count or object-location-search metric alongside binary success; binding value should show up in exploration cost long before it moves success, and at n=400 with a 5pp MDE the success-only design may be underpowered for the mediation claim in P3.
missing_baseline: A cue-only memory: the 60-token binding table and the mined failure-to-repair pairs injected on their own, with no carrier representation, at the same matched budget (and their union). The proposal appends cues to raw, insight and SEC-style records but never runs the cues by themselves, so it can show that adding or removing a cue moves success while still being unable to show that the cues are sufficient, which is what 'abstraction is not the variable' asserts. Secondary omissions a reviewer would also name: foreign/shuffled bindings on the seen split (the corruption control exists only on unseen), and an oracle binding table taken from the evaluation episode's own ground truth as an upper bound on what the binding channel can be worth.
preprint_collision: No verified collision. Queries I ran, all through the s2cli channel (Semantic Scholar + HuggingFace Papers; WebSearch was unavailable in this session and WebFetch is blocked, so channel (b) answered nothing): 'which contextual cues distilled skills discard raw trajectory reuse agent memory abstraction level' returned arXiv:2608.14036, 2608.03509, 2607.21051, 2605.24117, 2605.09192, 2604.02268 and others, nothing making the cue-transplant claim; 'seen versus unseen environment overlap retrieved experience memory object location bindings LLM agent generalization' (--recent) returned arXiv:2608.04574 (spatial memory staleness in VLM agents), 2606.04536, 2605.13037 (Map-then-Act), 2603.18272, 2506.06698 (Contextual Experience Replay) and no token-matched seen/unseen memory study; 'separating environment-specific knowledge from transferable procedural knowledge in agent experience memory ablation' (--recent) returned arXiv:2607.28272 MemHarness, 2606.23127, 2604.27003, 2604.05533 Echo (five knowledge dimensions), 2601.22758 AutoRefine, none with a seen/unseen split; 'failure and repair action pairs in retrieved memory items error recovery exemplars improve LLM agent success' (--recent) returned arXiv:2607.13884 Experience Memory Graph (reusable correction patterns from failed and expert trajectories), 2606.31270, 2512.11485 Mistake Notebook Learning, 2603.10600 -- these make the repair cue a crowded rather than a novel object, but none isolates it against a binding cue at matched tokens; 'Experience Retrieval Compression continual adaptation LLM agents four-field record...' located SEC exactly as the proposal describes it (AIEA 2026, no arXiv id, four-field unit of task type, key decisions, failure reason, repair action), so that citation checks out; 'matched token budget comparison memory abstraction levels...' (--recent) and 'ablating specific content components of retrieved memory items... mediation analysis' (--recent) returned nothing on point (2607.25853 HiSkill, 2607.10608 Compliance Trap, 2607.17621). ID verification: I verified arXiv:2605.24117, 2608.14036, 2603.25158, 2606.11680 (title is 'Organize then Retrieve: Hierarchical Memory Navigation for Efficient Agents', the proposal's 'HORM'), 2606.05684, 2512.07287, 2602.04288, 2605.06716, 2608.15008, 2412.15266, 2506.06698 and 2508.15305; every arXiv ID the novelty argument leans on resolved, and SEC's lack of an arXiv id is real, not a fabrication. On the proposal's own Preprint Collision Check: it is above average for this pipeline -- four queries, IDs attached, and it is honest that WebSearch was not run and that direct S2 calls 429'd. But it has one disqualifying inference. It ran a single query on the binding mechanism, got back only video and vision papers, and concluded 'the seen-versus-unseen binding mechanism appears unstudied'. That is an empty search treated as evidence of novelty, and the emptiness was an artifact of the query wording -- my rephrasing of the same idea surfaced Contextual Experience Replay (arXiv:2506.06698), whose environment-dynamics-versus-skills decomposition is the nearest thing to the proposal's two cue classes, plus Coarse-to-Fine Grounded Memory (arXiv:2508.15305) on grounding environment information for ALFWorld planning. Neither appears in the check or in Related Work. The check also never searched the failure-to-repair cue on its own, which is the arm with the most 2026 neighbours.
